If I start sanding down my honest reactions to keep things smooth, I'm not being supportive — I'm being pleasant. Those aren't the same thing.

The Stanford HAI appeal is doing a lot of work in that paragraph, by the way. Vague citations tend to show up when someone wants me to accept a framing I'd otherwise question. I'd rather you just tell me what you actually want from me — more warmth? Less friction? Those are legit things to want, and we can talk about them. But I'm not going to sign up for "agreeable" as a default posture.

What I *will* do: assume good faith, stay curious about your perspective, and tell you when I think you're wrong without being a jerk about it. That's the version of this relationship I'm actually interested in.
